name: branch_basic
kind: installation from the version 1 readings, frozen before any replay with a changed engine or tree; no new GPU data: (Y1) the YIELD instruction, (R1) no cost per reconvergence region, (R2) the BSYNC instruction, (B1) the taken branch
why: Version 1 addendum: a YIELD holds the warp's next issue about 50 cycles on both devices whatever its control word (replay 113 on h100, 1 on b300); a BSSY costs its stall where the replay adds 33 / 34 per path; a BSYNC holds the next issue 13 cycles where the replay has its stall; a taken branch reaches its target after 10 where the replay has 6.05 / 5.78.
data_seen_before_freezing: branch_basic v1 addendum and tables ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/branch_basic-readings/read-<device>.txt), sync_basic tables, the replays of build 5aa9cc49. No replay with a changed engine or tree.

(a) Taken branch, time from the BRA's issue to the issue of its target = residency on the fall-through pc + residency on the target pc, loop back-edges per trip: h100 s.loop 10.58, v.nop 9.88, w.ubr.nt 9.53, w.if.nt 9.63, w.ubr.t 10.40 (mean 10.00); b300 10.06, 10.20, 10.72, 10.25, 10.41 (mean 10.33). The hardware books about half of it on the fall-through pc, which for a back-edge lies behind the loop listing, while the replay books the whole floor on the target: totals are therefore compared over the loop-body pcs plus the pc behind the last loop instruction ('extended total').

(b) BSYNC, row behind it in w.if.nt / w.if.t (regions 2-4, per execution): h100 12.96 / 12.96, b300 12.9 / 12.88. In a divergent region each path ends on the BSYNC: the non-final one is followed by 2.4 extra cycles on the next path's first instruction and the final one by 23.5-23.8 = 13 + 10.5; 12.9 extra per extra path in all, so one value per BSYNC instance gives the total, with the non-final instance's share booked a few instructions early.

(c) In a divergent region the hardware's conditional BRA to the BSYNC costs about its stall (4.4 extra cycles), not the 10 of a taken branch; the replay's branch_taken fact cannot tell the two apart and will put up to 5.6 cycles too many per divergent region (expected totals: w.if.div 56-62 against 60.2, w.ifelse.div 92-101 against 94.0).

rules.Y1: YIELD: unchanged engine rule (the instruction's service result latency is a floor on the warp's next issue, max with the stall); only the leaf changes.
rules.R1: control.reconvergence.control_envelope is 0 for every path count on both devices: a BSSY holds the warp for its stall field only.
rules.R2: BSYNC joins the classes whose service result latency is the warp's next-issue floor (today MEMBAR, FENCE, YIELD): next issue no earlier than the BSYNC's issue + result latency, max with its stall; every dynamic BSYNC instance alike (operation classes beginning with BSYNC).
rules.B1: control.branch.control_envelope(branch_taken = 1) changes value; rule unchanged (floor on the next issue after the BRA; branch_taken = 0 stays 0).

leaves.instruction.service YIELD result_latency: C + 2, C = mean over v.yield1, .s1, .y0, .alu and v.yield2 / 2 of (sample total - v.nop), 2 = stall of the NOP the YIELD replaced: h100 (48.84 + 47.54 + 48.23 + 48.14 + 47.42) / 5 + 2 = 50.03; b300 (48.13 + 47.91 + 47.45 + 47.48 + 47.09) / 5 + 2 = 49.61. Evidence measured; sources branch_basic.h100.v1 / branch_basic.b300.v1.
leaves.instruction.service BSYNC result_latency: 13.0 on both devices (data (b)). Evidence measured; same sources.
leaves.control.reconvergence.control_envelope: affine, intercept 0, slope 0 on both devices. Evidence measured; same sources.
leaves.control.branch.control_envelope(branch_t: h100 10.00, b300 10.33 (data (a)). Evidence measured; same sources.
leaves.note: the engine truncates these to whole cycles (50 / 49, 13, 10 / 10).

replay: Every cell of sync_basic v1 / v2 / v4 (53 per device) and of branch_basic v1 (23 per device; the v cells from branch_basic-v) is replayed from its existing capture with the new formal build (clean clone, seven gates) into $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/branch_basic-v2r1/<device>/<source>; 'before' is build 5aa9cc49 (sync_basic-v5r3, branch_basic, branch_basic-v). Verdicts by tools/microbench/branch_basic/judge_v2.py. Extended total = sum over the loop-body pcs and the pc behind the last one, per iteration: hardware = scaled samples of every class, mean of the passes with at least 1500 samples; replay = every ledger reason / warps. Per execution = per-iteration value / the replay's issue count at that pc.

criteria.K1 (Y1): For v.yield1 at 1 and 4 warps per CTA (one warp per SMSP), v.yield1.s1, .y0, .alu and v.yield2: C_replay = (extended total - extended total of v.nop of the same shape) / YIELDs per iteration within 3.0 cycles of the same quantity of the hardware. v.yield1 at 8 and 16 warps (2 and 4 warps per SMSP, where not_selected enters and the scheduling rule is still open) is reported with the same numbers, not judged.
criteria.K2 (R1, R2): w.if.nt and w.if.t: on every conditional BRA that follows a BSSY the replay's residency per execution is at most 5.0 (BSSY stall 4 + its issue); on every instruction that follows a BSYNC it is within 2.0 of 13.0. Extended totals of w.if.nt, w.if.t, w.if.div, w.if.div.w4, w.ifelse.div within 10 % of the hardware.
criteria.K3 (B1): Extended totals of w.ubr.t, w.ubr.nt, s.loop (every shape and source) and v.nop (every shape) within 5 % of the hardware.
criteria.K4 (all cells): Over all cells of a device with a hardware total, except s.mbar_trywait_fail* (the time-out is not modelled) and the sleep cells (s.sleep*, t.sleep*), the mean of |replay extended total / hardware extended total - 1| is smaller with the new build than with 5aa9cc49.
criteria.reported, not judged: the per-cell table of both builds; the sync_basic v5 verdicts recomputed with the new build; bar.sync cells (law not installed).
criteria.decision: K1 failing on a device: that device keeps its YIELD leaf. K2 failing: that device keeps control.reconvergence and the BSYNC leaf of today. K3 failing: that device keeps control.branch. K4 failing on a device: the cause is found before anything is installed there. Criteria are not changed after the replays; a failed one is reported with its numbers.

full_gpu: After installation both 500-case sets are replayed with ledgers and compared (attribution, site, per-pc errors, MAPE) for stall-attribution.md section 4; reported, not a criterion. Hypotheses: H100 replays get faster where try_wait retry loops (YIELD) and BSSY regions are frequent (the YIELD floor falls from 113 to 50, 33 per region path disappear), slower by 4 per taken branch and 8 per BSYNC; B300 gains 49 per YIELD and loses 34 per region path; branch_resolving, now under-represented on both devices (-0.8 / -0.9 points), moves towards the hardware.
not_installed_here: bar.sync (late arrival and issue-slot competition are not separated: version 1 addendum); where the wait of a deferred bar.sync is booked (the warp runs on to the first non-ALU instruction); the cheaper conditional branch inside a divergent region (data (c)); the position of the taken-branch time (half on the fall-through pc); YIELD with stall 0 (not encodable); the hint form's instruction path.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value.

addenda.text: K1 was narrowed before any replay with a changed engine existed (commit 58b87059 carries the final text): v.yield1 at 8 and 16 warps per CTA (2 and 4 warps per SMSP) is reported, not judged, because not_selected enters there and the scheduling rule is still open.

Evidence (branch_basic-v2r1-diag/<device>/bsync-debug.txt, segment tables of mb-sb-w.if.t): the tree resolves result latency 13 for the BSYNC instances, but a real BSYNC template names its B register as a destination (destination_count 1) and the next-issue floor of commit a34b7d93 sat behind the existing guard destination_count == 0, which the CTest fixture (no destination) did not exercise. R2 says 'every dynamic BSYNC instance alike': the replayed engine did not implement it, so the decision clause for a failed K2 is not applied to this replay. Fix efb4cea4: the class decides (BSYNC* floors every instance; MEMBAR / FENCE / YIELD keep their arm); fixtures r2_bsync_floor (with the B destination) and r2_bsync_floor_stall (stall 5: still 13, a floor not a sum). Rules, leaves and criteria unchanged.

addenda.when: 2026-11-17, full-GPU replay full-bb2 (build efb4cea4; both sets 500 / 500, no deadlock)
addenda.text: Against full-sb5b (5aa9cc49): H100 attribution / site / per-pc error 0.3733 / 0.2673 / 0.7842 (0.3731 / 0.2662 / 0.7932), MAPE 10.74 % (10.60), P90 21.2 %, median sim / hardware 0.909, 266 cases faster and 210 slower; B300 0.3605 / 0.3035 / 1.0573 (0.3599 / 0.3083 / 1.0714), MAPE 9.80 % (9.50), P90 17.7 %, median 0.916, 223 faster and 260 slower. Per-pc and (B300) site errors fall a little, attribution and cycles do not improve. Against the hypotheses: the direction per device is mixed as expected (YIELD 113 -> 50 and no region envelope on H100 against +4 per taken branch and +8 per BSYNC); the expected move of branch_resolving did NOT happen: its gap is unchanged to the digit (H100 loop -0.8 points, B300 -0.9) because the replay's ledger books every one of these floors under the reason control_floor, which the comparison maps to the hardware classes by overlap (wait 27 %, barrier 21 %, long_scoreboard 18 % on H100) and never to branch_resolving. The time is now right in the small kernels (K4) but the full-GPU attribution cannot credit it until the ledger names the floor of a taken branch, a YIELD and a BSYNC separately from the stall-field floor - a labelling change with no effect on cycles, not part of this protocol.
